items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: My uncle Bay, he was always a baker, and they at Kresberries, and then a buyer at Sattlers and he used to call me up

ctx.x: Yes. And that’s after they kind of gave up a little bit on jazz, but there had to be something there that kept them with it. So here I was in school, and we were a nomadic tribe. We moved. It was like the Italians — and we weren’t alone with the Italians — but my father’s family, they were Sicilian, the Mancusos. And his father, and they had four kids, three boys and a girl. And they bought a house. You know, they were from Sicily. And they made sure that there was room for the sons. Okay? And as the sons got…
